documentTitle: Matcha On Ice Cafe — Syrups & Cold Foam

sections.label: Syrups
sections.blurb: The flavored syrups behind every Signature Matcha, made in-house.

drinks.name: Vanilla Syrup
method: Add the sugar and water to a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir until the sugar dissolves, then bring to a boil.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the vanilla bean paste and a pinch of salt.
Let cool, then transfer to a bottle or jar.
drinks.note: The pinch of salt isn't a mistake — it rounds out the sweetness and makes the vanilla taste even more like vanilla. Keeps refrigerated for about a month.

drinks.name: Banana Bread Syrup
method: Add the butter to a saucepan over medium heat. Add the mashed bananas and brown sugar.
Let caramelize for 2–3 minutes, then add the water, cinnamon and salt. Mix and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 7–10 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Let cool to room temperature, then blend or strain.
drinks.note: Store in an airtight jar and refrigerate for up to 3 weeks.

drinks.name: Strawberry Syrup
method: Add the strawberries, sugar and hot water to a pot.
Turn the heat to medium-high and stir to help dissolve the sugar.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 8 minutes.
Remove from heat and blend with an immersion blender until smooth.
Let cool, then transfer to a jar or bottle.

drinks.name: Caramel Syrup
method: Warm the cream (stovetop or microwave) and set aside.
Combine the sugar and water in a saucepan over medium heat. Don't stir — swirl the pan occasionally to help it dissolve evenly.
Cook until the sugar turns a deep amber color, watching closely — it can go from amber to burnt in seconds.
Remove from heat and carefully whisk in the warm cream — it will bubble vigorously.
Whisk in the butter and salt until smooth.
Let cool, then transfer to a bottle or jar.
drinks.note: A lightly salted caramel. Keeps refrigerated for about 2 weeks; warm slightly if it thickens too much in the fridge.

drinks.name: Honey Cinnamon Syrup
method: Combine the honey, water and cinnamon sticks in a saucepan over low-medium heat.
Warm gently, stirring to dissolve the honey into the water — do not boil, to protect the honey's flavor.
Once combined, remove from heat and let the cinnamon steep for 15–20 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon sticks, stir in a pinch of salt, then let cool.
Transfer to a bottle or jar.

drinks.name: Mango Syrup
method: Peel and chop the mango, then blend until smooth to make a purée — a small splash of water helps it along, if needed.
Pour the purée into a saucepan, add the sugar and water, and stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, whisking continuously until the sugar fully dissolves.
Remove from heat and let cool completely.
Transfer to a clean bottle or airtight container.
drinks.note: Store refrigerated for up to 2 weeks — shake well before each use.

sections.label: Cold Foam
sections.blurb: The base cold foam used across the Signature Matchas.

story.heading: About Cold Foam
body: Cold foam comes together from three components: two parts Heavy Cream, which brings fat, creaminess and structure; one part Whole Milk, which lightens the texture; and one part Syrup or purée, which brings flavor, sugar and liquid.
It's built in two stages. First, air is whipped into the mixture, so it gains volume and grows in size. Then that air is textured into the base, giving the foam its velvety, light finish.

callout.label: Base Ratio
callout.note: For every 4 oz of base — 2 oz heavy cream, 1 oz whole milk, 1 oz syrup or purée.

method: Combine the heavy cream, whole milk and syrup in a 2:1:1 ratio.
Whip to incorporate air — the mixture will grow in volume.
Continue whipping to texture that air into the base, until velvety and light.
Batch ahead of the shift and keep refrigerated for quick service.

sections.label: Seasonal Add-Ons
sections.blurb: Fall Collection — Pumpkin & Brown Sugar: a rotating set of seasonal syrups, sauces and cold foams.
sections.endcardBody: This chapter stays open. New seasonal syrups, sauces and cold foams take their place here as each collection launches, with its own page in this document.

drinks.name: Brown Sugar Syrup
method: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, whisk together the brown sugar and water. Add the cinnamon sticks. Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve the sugar.
Reduce heat and simmer about 2 minutes, until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Remove from heat and cool completely. Remove the cinnamon sticks, pour into a glass jar, and store in the refrigerator.
drinks.note: Cooling before straining lets the cinnamon keep infusing the syrup.

drinks.name: Pumpkin Spice Sauce

ingredients.item: Water (1 cup for a thicker sauce)
Vanilla Bean Paste — add off heat

method: Combine the brown sugar, maple syrup, pumpkin purée, water, pumpkin pie spice, cinnamon and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a low simmer and cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla bean paste.
drinks.note: 2 cups water = thinner, pourable syrup. 1 cup water = thicker sauce.

drinks.name: Salted Maple Cold Foam
method: Combine the heavy cream, whole milk, maple syrup and salt in a blender or with a milk frother.
Whip until light and foamy but still pourable — thick enough to float on top of a drink.
drinks.note: 2:1:1 (cream:milk:flavor) is the base ratio for every cold foam on the menu.

drinks.name: Pumpkin Pie Cold Foam

ingredients.item: Pumpkin Pie Spice — for visible flecks

method: Combine the heavy cream, whole milk, Pumpkin Spice Sauce, salt and pumpkin pie spice in a blender or with a milk frother.
Whip until light and foamy but still pourable — thick enough to float on top of a drink.
Dust with an extra pinch of pumpkin pie spice on top right before serving, for visible flecks and aroma.
drinks.note: Pumpkin Spice Sauce already carries sweetness and spice — it swaps 1:1 for maple syrup in the base ratio.
